title: Low contrast in code windows across the app, especially red/green diff highlights
scope:
# Summary

Code windows across the app have too-low contrast, making code hard to read. It is especially bad where red/green diff highlights are applied, and gets worse when viewing the monitor from more than a couple of feet away. This is an accessibility issue.

# Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any code window in the app (e.g. a diff/review view).
2. View code, particularly lines with red/green added/removed diff highlights.
3. Step back a few feet from the monitor.

Expected: Code text is comfortably readable against both the base background and diff highlight backgrounds, including at a normal viewing distance.
Actual: Contrast is too low; text over red/green highlights is very hard to read, worse at distance.

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Code text meets WCAG AA contrast (≥ 4.5:1) against the base code background
- [ ] Code text over added/removed diff-line highlights meets WCAG AA contrast (≥ 4.5:1)
- [ ] Added vs. removed diff highlights remain distinguishable and readable at typical viewing distance
- [ ] Verified in both light and dark themes

# Dev Hints

* Review the code/diff theme colors app-wide; verify foreground text contrast against both the base background and the added/removed highlight backgrounds.
* Use the existing `--tm-*` design tokens rather than hard-coded colors.
